name: DATE2024 SELL SpMV required indexed-vector staging
summary: Programmed required indirect read staging into L2 scratchpad, followed by ordinary AXI4 Ara consumer loads. Scope is the published SELL SpMV path.

result.form: Indexed-vector operand stream densely staged in configured L2 scratchpad arrays; transport returns original narrow-request order.
result.validity: Required operands; exact host-visible per-tile readiness event and padded-lane handling unknown.

ordering.description: Restores original narrow-request ordering after block coalescing; no global memory or arbitrary cross-ID ordering guarantee.

completion.event: Transport responses and application pointer-depleted/result-full refresh are described; exact gather-ready/final-drain event not exposed.
completion.visibility: Destination-ready, software barrier, final output visibility and consumer-release ABI unknown.

realization.description: CVA6 configures L2 staging and Ara consumes it over ordinary AXI4. CPU/VPC multiply-add, output ownership and result drain remain outside this gather operation.

operations.datatype_notes: 32-bit indices and 64-bit nonzeros/metadata are evaluated widths; do not infer all signedness, element/index type domains or arithmetic safety.
limitations: No general scatter, duplicate-write ordering, coherent atomics or inherited DATE2023 ISA path.
No authenticated publication-specific RTL or staging driver ABI.

interface.software_supplies: CVA6 configures contiguous/indirect L2-SPM staging for SELL tiles. Source/destination register/descriptor encoding unavailable.
interface.invocation: Programmed first-tile staging followed by overlapped later tile refill; no invented function or register layout.
interface.outputs: Required indexed-vector values in L2 for ordinary Ara loads. SpMV arithmetic, result output and final drain are separate responsibilities.

internal_mechanisms.description: Wide index fetches feed N parallel index queues and dependent narrow element request generation.
W oldest narrow requests form a parallel comparison window; N,W powers of two, W>=N; single CSHR aggregates same-block hits.
Hitmap and per-position offset queues associate wide responses with narrow consumers; W element queues and downsizer enforce original order before packing.
Regulator timeout forwards an incomplete window; separate watcher watchdog issues a pending coalesced wide request.
Six L2 arrays hold slice pointers, results, double-buffered nonzeros and indexed vectors; execution interrupts on pointer depletion or full result array and signals refresh.

limitations: Only the DATE2024 paper-scoped mapping; not DATE2023 direct vector-register integration.
Parameter domains, translations/coherence, final partial/drain, faults and result lifetime remain open.

performance_hypotheses.description: Requests sharing a DRAM block within the finite W window may reduce transferred blocks while L2 staging overlaps vector computation. This is a mechanism hypothesis, not a cross-design ranking.
workload_conditions: Published tiled SELL SpMV operand staging; configured L2 arrays and source lifetime must hold.
Enough same-block requests inside W and overlap opportunity for subsequent tile staging.
limiting_factors: Window/FIFO capacity, request diversity, partial-window progress and payload-transfer costs.
Unresolved first/final tile readiness, reuse and result-drain interface.
